neighboringSourceContext.speaker: Jonathan Haidt
neighboringSourceContext.claimSummary: More flourishing is better other things equal, but a life's value is not exhausted by summing pleasurable or happy moments because narrative and meaning also matter.
neighboringSourceContext.reasonSummary: A life with substantially more happy moments can nevertheless be evaluated as an utter failure in its final narrative; people care about purpose and the story of the whole life.

inferenceSummary.premise: People's considered evaluation of lives depends on meaning and narrative as well as momentary experience.
inferenceSummary.inference: A metric that simply aggregates experiential moments can rank lives incorrectly.
inferenceSummary.conclusion: Well-being understood as summed experience is insufficient as a complete moral criterion.

neighboringSourceContext.speaker: Jonathan Haidt
neighboringSourceContext.claimSummary: Meaning, purpose, and accomplishment are not captured merely by asking how much happiness the remembered self reports.
neighboringSourceContext.reasonSummary: Haidt distinguishes the value-laden structure of a life from remembered quantities of happiness.

inferenceSummary.premise: A person can assess purpose and accomplishment separately from remembered happiness.
inferenceSummary.inference: Expanding the time horizon of happiness measurement does not automatically incorporate those goods.
inferenceSummary.conclusion: The remembered-self distinction leaves the sufficiency objection alive.

neighboringSourceContext.speaker: Sam Harris
neighboringSourceContext.claimSummary: Meaning, connection, and life story can be included within the thing measured as well-being, even when attaining them reduces momentary pleasure.
neighboringSourceContext.reasonSummary: People do not seek the pleasure profile of successful heroin addicts; they willingly undergo ordeals for connection, meaning, and a good story, all of which affect the total value under the curve.

inferenceSummary.premise: Considered human flourishing includes meaning, connection, and narrative, not merely pleasure.
inferenceSummary.inference: A well-being measure can track those experienced and reflective goods and their trade-offs.
inferenceSummary.conclusion: Meaning complicates measurement but need not constitute an independent moral foundation.
